brief: The ultimate guide to display type — 6 rules that make headlines unforgettable.

slots.body: Six rules to make your headlines bold, beautiful, and impossible to ignore.

slots.title: Scale Until It Screams
slots.body: Display type lives at the top of the visual hierarchy. If your headline isn't the biggest element on the page, the layout has already failed.

slots.title: Pair With Purpose
slots.body: Combine a bold sans serif with an elegant italic serif. The tension between the two creates energy and guides the reader's eye exactly where you want it.

slots.title: Let It Breathe
slots.body: Generous margins and line height are not wasted pixels. White space is the frame that turns loud typography into sophisticated, digestible art.
slots.quote: Silence speaks as loud as type.

slots.title: Limit Your Fonts
slots.body: One type family with multiple weights is often enough. Adding a third font rarely adds charm; it usually adds confusion and dilutes your message.
slots.quote: Two fonts sing, three fonts shout.

slots.title: Use Color as Voice
slots.body: A single burnt orange word against cream commands more attention than a rainbow paragraph. Use accent color like a spotlight, not a floodlight.
slots.quote: One accent beats a hundred hues.

slots.title: Clarity Beats Clever
slots.body: Decorative ligatures and extreme tracking mean nothing if the headline can't be read in a glance. Legibility is the non-negotiable foundation of display type.
slots.quote: If they pause, you've lost them.

slots.body: Apply these six rules to your next layout and watch ordinary text transform into typographic power.
